clue_en: This barrier contraceptive is worn during sex and also reduces the spread of many infections.
explanation_en: A condom is a barrier contraceptive that can also reduce infection risk.

clue_en: This pharmacy product checks urine for hCG and can be used without visiting a laboratory.
explanation_en: A home pregnancy test detects hCG in urine.

clue_en: This reusable, usually bell-shaped menstrual product collects fluid rather than absorbing it.
explanation_en: A menstrual cup is a reusable product that collects menstrual fluid.

clue_en: Folic acid is a key ingredient in this supplement commonly taken before and during pregnancy.
explanation_en: Prenatal vitamins commonly include folic acid.

clue_en: Kotex helped popularize this absorbent menstrual product after the First World War.
explanation_en: A sanitary pad is an absorbent menstrual product; Kotex became an early mass-market brand.

clue_en: This stage of development brings sexual maturity and secondary sex characteristics.
explanation_en: Puberty is the developmental transition to sexual maturity.

clue_en: This recurring process sheds the uterine lining when pregnancy has not occurred.
explanation_en: Menstruation is the recurring shedding of the uterine lining.

clue_en: Around the middle of many menstrual cycles, this process releases an egg from an ovary.
explanation_en: Ovulation is the release of an egg from an ovary.

clue_en: Gestation is the more technical word for this period between conception and birth.
explanation_en: Pregnancy is the period from conception through birth.

clue_en: Doctors identify this life-stage transition retrospectively after 12 consecutive months without menstruation.
explanation_en: Menopause is identified after 12 consecutive months without menstruation.

clue_en: This two-time Nobel laureate helped develop mobile X-ray units during the First World War.
explanation_en: Marie Curie helped create mobile X-ray units during the First World War.

clue_en: Known as the Lady with the Lamp, this nurse became a symbol of modern nursing.
explanation_en: Florence Nightingale became known as the Lady with the Lamp and helped shape modern nursing.

clue_en: Pasteurization takes its name from this French scientist associated with germ theory.
explanation_en: Louis Pasteur's work on microbes gave pasteurization its name.

clue_en: A newborn's condition is quickly summarized by a five-part score named for this American physician.
explanation_en: Virginia Apgar developed the newborn assessment that bears her name.

clue_en: In 1849, this physician became the first woman to receive a medical degree in the United States.
explanation_en: Elizabeth Blackwell became the first woman to earn a medical degree in the United States when Geneva Medical College awarded her an M.D. in 1849.

clue_en: In sexual reproduction, this familiar female gamete can unite with a sperm cell.
explanation_en: An egg is the female gamete in many forms of sexual reproduction.

clue_en: This typically mobile male gamete carries half the chromosomes needed for fertilization.
explanation_en: A sperm cell is a male gamete carrying half a typical chromosome set.

clue_en: Bees often assist this process by moving pollen from one flower to another.
explanation_en: Pollination transfers pollen between flower structures.

clue_en: In this marine fish, the male carries developing young in a brood pouch.
explanation_en: Male seahorses carry developing young in a brood pouch.

clue_en: If the dominant female disappears from its reef group, a breeding male of this orange-and-white fish can change sex and take her place.
explanation_en: Clownfish live in social groups with a breeding female. If she dies, the dominant male can change sex and become the new breeding female.

clue_en: Often simply called the pill, this contraceptive is taken by mouth on a schedule.
explanation_en: The birth control pill is an oral contraceptive.

clue_en: This skin-worn contraceptive releases hormones through an adhesive square.
explanation_en: A contraceptive patch delivers hormones through the skin.

clue_en: Usually abbreviated IUD, this small contraceptive device is placed inside the uterus.
explanation_en: An intrauterine device is placed in the uterus for contraception.

clue_en: This dome-shaped barrier contraceptive is placed over the cervix before sex.
explanation_en: A contraceptive diaphragm covers the cervix as a barrier.

clue_en: This contraceptive procedure blocks or cuts the vas deferens.
explanation_en: A vasectomy interrupts the vas deferens.

clue_en: This word means a voluntary agreement to an action or proposal.
explanation_en: Consent is voluntary agreement.

clue_en: A clinician writes this authorization before a pharmacy dispenses many medicines.
explanation_en: A prescription authorizes a pharmacy to dispense a medicine.

clue_en: This broad term covers information and services that help people decide whether and when to have children.
explanation_en: Family planning supports decisions about whether and when to have children.

clue_en: Medical confidentiality protects this personal sphere of information and choice.
explanation_en: Privacy includes control over personal information and choices.

clue_en: Vaccination campaigns and clean-water programmes belong to this field focused on whole communities rather than one patient.
explanation_en: Public health aims to protect and improve health across communities.

clue_en: Folklore often shows this long-legged bird delivering babies in a bundle.
explanation_en: The stork is a traditional folklore symbol of delivering babies.

clue_en: At this pre-birth celebration, guests commonly give gifts for the expected child.
explanation_en: A baby shower celebrates an expected child with gifts.

clue_en: Mia Farrow plays a pregnant Manhattan woman who fears her neighbors have plans for her baby in this 1968 film.
explanation_en: Rosemary's Baby is a 1968 psychological horror film starring Mia Farrow as a pregnant Manhattan woman who suspects a sinister plot involving her baby.

clue_en: This BBC drama follows nurses and midwives in London's East End beginning in the 1950s.
explanation_en: Call the Midwife is a BBC period drama about nurses and midwives.

clue_en: This bestselling pregnancy guide by Heidi Murkoff uses a repeated form of the verb expect in its title.
response_en: What to Expect When You're Expecting
explanation_en: What to Expect When You're Expecting is a bestselling pregnancy guide.
source_title: What to Expect When You're Expecting — Wikipedia

clue_en: This trained professional supports people through pregnancy, birth, and early postnatal care.
explanation_en: A midwife provides care during pregnancy, birth, and after delivery.

clue_en: Calculated from pregnancy timing, this estimated calendar point is not a guarantee of the baby's birthday.
explanation_en: A due date estimates when a baby may be born.

clue_en: Often shortened to C-section, this operation delivers a baby through incisions in the abdomen and uterus.
explanation_en: A cesarean section delivers a baby surgically through the abdomen and uterus.

clue_en: These rhythmic tightenings of the uterus help move labor toward birth.
explanation_en: Labor contractions are rhythmic uterine tightenings that help the cervix open and move birth forward.

clue_en: During labour, pain medicine may be delivered through a catheter near the spine using this technique.
explanation_en: An epidural can deliver pain relief near the spinal nerves during labour.

clue_en: This ribbon colour is widely associated with breast-cancer awareness.
explanation_en: The pink ribbon is associated with breast-cancer awareness.

clue_en: Anna Jarvis campaigned for this family observance, celebrated on the second Sunday of May in many countries.
explanation_en: Anna Jarvis promoted Mother's Day in the United States.

clue_en: This coloured loop is an international symbol of HIV and AIDS awareness.
explanation_en: The red ribbon symbolizes HIV and AIDS awareness.

clue_en: Observed on December 1, this international day focuses attention on HIV and AIDS.
explanation_en: World AIDS Day is observed on December 1.

clue_en: The numbers 28 and 5 shape the date of this May awareness day: an average cycle is often described as 28 days and menstruation as five days.
explanation_en: Menstrual Hygiene Day is observed on May 28, using 28 and 5 as symbolic cycle figures.

clue_en: A dentist may use this image to see decay hidden inside a tooth.
explanation_en: Dental X-rays reveal structures and decay that cannot be seen during an ordinary visual examination.

clue_en: This imaging method uses high-frequency sound waves and is familiar from pregnancy scans.
explanation_en: Ultrasound imaging uses high-frequency sound waves.

clue_en: Insulin and estrogen are examples of this kind of chemical messenger in the body.
explanation_en: Hormones are chemical messengers; insulin and estrogen are examples.

clue_en: A vaccine trains the immune system to recognize targets partly through these Y-shaped proteins.
explanation_en: Antibodies are Y-shaped immune proteins that bind targets.

clue_en: This small device clips onto a fingertip and uses light to estimate blood oxygen saturation and pulse rate.
explanation_en: A pulse oximeter uses light passing through a fingertip or other thin body part to estimate oxygen saturation and pulse rate without drawing blood.

clue_en: This marriage system joins one person to one spouse at a time.
explanation_en: Monogamy is marriage to one spouse at a time.

clue_en: A couple who share a home and domestic life without being married are in this arrangement.
explanation_en: Cohabitation means two people living together as a couple without being married; its legal effects differ by jurisdiction.

clue_en: A 40th wedding anniversary traditionally takes the name of this red gemstone.
explanation_en: The 40th wedding anniversary is the ruby anniversary.

clue_en: In Fiddler on the Roof, Yente practices this profession of arranging introductions for marriage.
explanation_en: A matchmaker brings together prospective partners.
source_title: Fiddler on the Roof — Music Theatre International

clue_en: In this property custom, assets are transferred from a bride's family to the couple or groom.
explanation_en: A dowry transfers property from the bride's family at marriage.

clue_en: Couples traditionally cut this decorated dessert together at their reception.
explanation_en: A wedding cake is a decorated reception dessert traditionally cut by the couple.

clue_en: A reception DJ may invite only the newlyweds onto the floor for this traditional spotlight moment.
explanation_en: The first dance traditionally opens the reception dance floor for the couple.

clue_en: Unmarried guests gather behind the bride before flowers fly over her shoulder in this custom.
explanation_en: The bouquet toss invites guests to catch the bride's flowers.

clue_en: When glasses rise, a speaker offers the couple a few ceremonial words in this reception ritual.
explanation_en: A wedding toast combines raised drinks with words honouring the couple.

clue_en: One wedding-party member may safeguard the rings, sign as a witness, and speak for the groom.
explanation_en: The best man traditionally assists the groom and may safeguard the rings.

clue_en: This quality helps partners stay calm when change or compromise takes time.
explanation_en: Patience is the ability to tolerate delay or difficulty without becoming upset.

clue_en: Partners may meet a trained counselor together in this form of therapy.
explanation_en: Couples therapy helps partners work on relationship concerns with a trained therapist.

clue_en: The Netherlands has offered couples this officially recorded relationship status since 1998.
explanation_en: Registered partnerships have been available to couples in the Netherlands since 1998.
source_title: LGBTI equality in the Netherlands — Government of the Netherlands

clue_en: This marriage payment moves from a groom or his family to the bride's family.
explanation_en: Bride price is wealth transferred by a groom's side to a bride's family.

clue_en: Fraternal forms of this marriage system join one woman to brothers.
explanation_en: Polyandry describes a woman having more than one husband.

clue_en: In many jurisdictions, a couple obtains this document before a legal wedding.
explanation_en: A marriage license authorizes a couple to marry under local law.

clue_en: A judge, registrar, or other state official may conduct this nonreligious wedding.
explanation_en: A civil ceremony is a nonreligious legal wedding conducted by an authorized official.

clue_en: This circular piece of jewellery commonly symbolizes a married commitment.
explanation_en: A wedding ring is a common symbol of marriage.

clue_en: In Britain, couples can marry at this local government office without a religious service.
explanation_en: A registry office records civil status and can host civil marriages in Britain.

clue_en: This post-wedding trip takes its English name from words associated with sweetness and a lunar month.
explanation_en: A honeymoon is a trip or holiday taken soon after a wedding.

clue_en: Italian speakers use this familiar word for love.
explanation_en: Amore is the Italian word for love.

clue_en: This two-word French phrase literally means my love.
explanation_en: Mon amour is French for my love.

clue_en: English borrowed this French word for a man engaged to be married.
explanation_en: Fiancé is the French-derived word for a man engaged to marry.

clue_en: In Hawaiian, this word can express love as well as greeting and farewell.
explanation_en: Aloha can express love, greeting, or farewell in Hawaiian.

clue_en: Wendy's family name in Peter Pan is also this English word of affection.
explanation_en: Darling is an English term of affection and the surname of Wendy and her family in J. M. Barrie's Peter Pan.

category_name_en: Breaking Up in Culture and Law
clue_en: This legal process ends a marriage.
explanation_en: Divorce legally ends a marriage.

category_name_en: Breaking Up in Culture and Law
clue_en: Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver play a separating couple in this 2019 film.
explanation_en: Marriage Story is a 2019 drama film starring Scarlett Johansson and Adam Driver as a couple going through divorce.

category_name_en: Breaking Up in Culture and Law
clue_en: Dustin Hoffman and Meryl Streep played divorcing parents in this 1979 Best Picture winner.
explanation_en: Kramer vs. Kramer is a 1979 drama about divorce and custody.

category_name_en: Breaking Up in Culture and Law
clue_en: After a separation, one former spouse may be ordered to make these support payments to the other.
explanation_en: Alimony is financial support paid to a former spouse.

category_name_en: Breaking Up in Culture and Law
clue_en: This contract agreed before a wedding sets financial terms that may apply if the marriage later ends.
explanation_en: A prenuptial agreement is a contract made before marriage that sets financial rights and responsibilities.

category_name_en: Dating Before and After the Internet
clue_en: Named after dry material used to start a fire, this dating app popularized swiping profiles.
explanation_en: Tinder is a dating app whose name also means dry fire-starting material.

category_name_en: Dating Before and After the Internet
clue_en: On this kind of date, the two people have not met before.
explanation_en: A blind date brings together people who have not previously met.

category_name_en: Dating Before and After the Internet
clue_en: Participants rotate through several very short conversations at this matchmaking event.
explanation_en: Speed dating uses a series of brief timed conversations.

category_name_en: Dating Before and After the Internet
clue_en: At formal balls, partners once wrote their names on this small schedule of promised dances.
explanation_en: A dance card recorded a person's promised dance partners.

category_name_en: Dating Before and After the Internet
clue_en: Launched in 1995, this service became one of the first major internet dating sites.
explanation_en: Match.com launched in 1995 as an early major dating website.

clue_en: In English-language correspondence, this character can represent a kiss.
explanation_en: The letter X is conventionally used to symbolize a kiss in messages.

clue_en: Before texting, a handwritten message of affection often took this form.
explanation_en: A love letter is a written expression of affection addressed to a romantic partner or interest.

clue_en: In older courtship customs, this supervising adult accompanied an unmarried couple.
explanation_en: A chaperone traditionally accompanied an unmarried couple to supervise social conduct.

clue_en: A short newspaper notice seeking a partner was traditionally called this.
explanation_en: A personal advertisement is a notice placed in a publication by someone seeking friendship or a romantic partner.

clue_en: During the 20th century, this Nevada city became known for short-residency divorces.
explanation_en: Reno attracted divorce seekers because Nevada required relatively short residency.

clue_en: Geoffrey Chaucer's Parliament of Fowls helped connect romantic love with this February observance.
explanation_en: Valentine's Day became associated with courtly romance in late medieval literature.

clue_en: At this kind of gathering, parents may display profiles of their unmarried adult children.
explanation_en: A marriage market is a social setting where families seek potential spouses for unmarried adults.

clue_en: OkCupid may display this number to summarize how closely two users' answers and preferences align.
explanation_en: OkCupid calculates a match percentage from users' answers, the importance they assign to those answers, and profile preferences.

clue_en: Gary Chapman published this relationship book in 1992.
explanation_en: The Five Love Languages was published by Gary Chapman in 1992.

clue_en: A message ending a romance, especially one sent to a distant serviceman, is known by this two-name phrase.
explanation_en: A Dear John letter is a written message telling a romantic partner, historically often a serviceman, that the relationship is over.

clue_en: This foundation of a relationship means confidence in another person's reliability and honesty.
explanation_en: Trust is confidence in another person's reliability and honesty.

clue_en: Listening and expressing needs clearly are parts of this two-way relationship skill.
explanation_en: Communication includes listening and expressing information clearly.

clue_en: When partners each give up part of what they want to reach agreement, they make this.
explanation_en: A compromise reaches agreement through mutual concessions.

clue_en: This ability involves understanding and sharing another person's feelings rather than merely solving the problem.
explanation_en: Empathy is the capacity to understand or share another person's feelings.

clue_en: In relationship language, this personal limit tells others what behaviour or contact a person will and will not accept.
explanation_en: A personal boundary defines acceptable behaviour or contact.

clue_en: The Human Rights Campaign places this mathematical mark in yellow on a blue square.
explanation_en: The Human Rights Campaign logo uses a yellow equal sign on a blue background as a symbol of equality.

clue_en: This pale-purple color lent its name both to a Cold War-era U.S. purge of gay federal employees and to marriages used to conceal sexual orientation.
explanation_en: Lavender became associated with homosexuality in English-language culture: the Lavender Scare names a U.S. purge of gay federal employees, while a lavender marriage is a marriage used to conceal sexual orientation.

clue_en: Once used by Nazis to mark prisoners, this shape was later reclaimed by gay-rights activists.
explanation_en: A pink triangle is a symbol for the LGBTQ+ community. Initially intended as a badge of shame, it was later reappropriated as a positive symbol of self-identity.

clue_en: Daniel Quasar added a chevron of trans-flag colors plus black and brown stripes to create this 2018 design.
explanation_en: Daniel Quasar designed the Progress Pride Flag in 2018 by adding a chevron of trans-flag colors and black and brown stripes to the rainbow flag.

clue_en: The Gay Activists Alliance adopted this Greek letter as a symbol in 1970.
explanation_en: The Gay Activists Alliance adopted the Greek letter lambda as a gay-rights symbol in 1970.

clue_en: This coming-of-age drama about Chiron won the 2017 Oscar for Best Picture.
explanation_en: Barry Jenkins's Moonlight follows Chiron as he grows up and won the 2017 Academy Award for Best Picture.

clue_en: Nick and Charlie are the central couple in this Alice Oseman comic and Netflix series.
explanation_en: Heartstopper is a British coming-of-age romantic comedy-drama television series created and written by Alice Oseman for Netflix, based on her webcomic and graphic novel series of the same name. Starring Kit Connor and Joe Locke as Nick Nelson and Charlie Spring, it follows two teenagers whose friendship at Truham Grammar School develops into a romantic relationship.

clue_en: Virginia Woolf's novel follows a poet who lives for centuries and changes sex.
explanation_en: The protagonist of Virginia Woolf's Orlando lives for centuries, changes sex, and works as a poet across different eras.

clue_en: Ballroom culture and chosen families drive this TV drama set in 1980s and 1990s New York.
explanation_en: Pose (stylized in all caps) is an American drama television series about New York City's ball culture, an LGBTQ subculture in the African-American and Latino communities, throughout the 1980s and 1990s. Featured characters are dancers and models, who compete for trophies and recognition in this underground culture and who support one another in a network of chosen families known as Houses.

clue_en: Alison Bechdel subtitled this graphic memoir 'A Family Tragicomic.'
explanation_en: Alison Bechdel's graphic memoir Fun Home: A Family Tragicomic explores the author's family, sexuality, and relationship with her father.

clue_en: This major English seaside Pride festival fills Brighton and Hove each summer.
explanation_en: Brighton Pride is an annual LGBT pride event held in the English seaside city of Brighton and Hove.

clue_en: The Chueca district and a huge march through Spain's capital identify this annual Pride festival.
explanation_en: Madrid Pride is an annual LGBTQ festival centered on Chueca and a major parade through Madrid.

clue_en: Canal Pride sends decorated boats through this European capital's waterways as part of this festival.
explanation_en: Amsterdam Pride includes Canal Pride, a boat parade through Amsterdam's canals.

clue_en: Avenida Paulista hosts this annual Brazilian Pride event.
explanation_en: São Paulo Pride is an annual LGBTQ Pride parade held on Avenida Paulista in São Paulo, Brazil.
source_title: São Paulo Gay Pride Parade — Wikipedia

clue_en: This organization runs the Canadian city's annual festival around Church and Wellesley.
explanation_en: Pride Toronto organizes Toronto's annual pride festival, including events around Church and Wellesley.

clue_en: He, she, and they are examples of these words that may appear beside a person's name in a profile.
explanation_en: Preferred gender pronouns (also called personal gender pronouns, often abbreviated as PGP) are the set of pronouns (in English, third-person pronouns) that an individual wants others to use to reflect that person's own gender identity.

clue_en: This phrase means voluntarily telling others about one's sexual orientation or gender identity.
explanation_en: Coming out of the closet, often shortened to coming out, is a metaphor mostly used to describe LGBTQ people's self-disclosure of their sexual orientation, romantic orientation, or gender identity.

clue_en: In social movements, this word describes a supporter who is not a member of the marginalized group.
explanation_en: Allyship is an English-language neologism used in contemporary social justice activism to describe efforts by groups of people to advance the interests of marginalized groups both in society at large and in particular social contexts, for example universities or workplaces.

clue_en: Close friends who provide family-like support may be called this two-word phrase.
explanation_en: Chosen family—also referred to as found family, or a family of choice—refers to non-biological kinship bonds that are intentionally formed, regardless of legal recognition. These relationships are often based on mutual care, support, and emotional connection.

clue_en: This one-word term combines death with a name for the former name others may use after a transgender person changes it.
explanation_en: Deadnaming means referring to a transgender or non-binary person by a former name they no longer use.

clue_en: Gilbert Baker created the first version of this LGBTQ pride symbol in 1978.
accepted_variants_en: Pride flag;Gay pride flag;LGBTQ pride flag
explanation_en: Gilbert Baker designed a rainbow pride flag in 1978.

clue_en: Rainbow flags and public celebration fill the streets during this march for LGBTQ visibility.
explanation_en: A pride parade is a public march and celebration supporting LGBTQ visibility, rights, and community.

clue_en: Pride colors painted across a pedestrian crossing create this public symbol of LGBTQ inclusion.
explanation_en: A rainbow crossing is a pedestrian crossing painted in rainbow colors as a public expression of LGBTQ Pride or inclusion.

clue_en: In 2019, this jurisdiction became the first in Asia to legalize same-sex marriage.
explanation_en: Taiwan implemented same-sex marriage in 2019.

clue_en: Founded in New York in 1987, this direct-action group responded to the AIDS crisis.
explanation_en: ACT UP was founded in New York City in 1987.

clue_en: This drag performer produces, hosts, and judges the reality competition series Drag Race.
explanation_en: RuPaul produces, hosts, and judges RuPaul's Drag Race, a reality competition series built around drag performance.

clue_en: Her sitcom character said 'Yep, I'm gay' in a highly watched 1997 episode.
explanation_en: In the highly watched 1997 Puppy Episode of Ellen, Ellen DeGeneres's sitcom character said, “Yep, I'm gay.”

clue_en: Playing Sophia Burset in Orange Is the New Black made this actress the first openly transgender person nominated for a Primetime Emmy in an acting category.
explanation_en: Laverne Cox played Sophia Burset in Orange Is the New Black and in 2014 became the first openly transgender person nominated for a Primetime Emmy acting award.

clue_en: This activist and self-described drag queen became a symbol of the Stonewall era.
explanation_en: Marsha P. Johnson was a gay-liberation activist, self-described drag queen, and prominent figure associated with the Stonewall era.

clue_en: This openly gay strategist organized the 1963 March on Washington.
explanation_en: Bayard Rustin, an openly gay civil-rights strategist, was the principal organizer of the 1963 March on Washington.

clue_en: In the United States, this observance fills the calendar each June.
explanation_en: Pride Month is a month-long celebration of LGBTQ communities and their contributions; in the United States it is observed in June in connection with the anniversary of the 1969 Stonewall uprising.

clue_en: Michael Page created this pink, purple, and blue flag in 1998.
explanation_en: The bisexual flag, also called the bisexual pride flag, is a pride flag representing bisexuality, bisexual individuals and the bisexual community. According to Michael Page, the activist who created the flag based on a color palette designed by Liz Nania, the pink stripe represents attraction to the same sex, while the blue stripe represents attraction to the opposite sex.

clue_en: This Israeli singer won the 1998 Eurovision Song Contest with 'Diva.'
explanation_en: Dana International won the 1998 Eurovision Song Contest for Israel with the song 'Diva.'

clue_en: Rome hosted the first edition of this international Pride festival in 2000.
explanation_en: Rome hosted the first WorldPride in 2000, establishing the international Pride festival named in the clue.

clue_en: Beginning in 1965, organizers gave this two-word name to a yearly July 4 picket at Independence Hall intended to remind Americans that gay citizens lacked basic civil rights.
explanation_en: The Annual Reminder was held at Independence Hall each July 4 from 1965 to 1969 to remind Americans that gay people were denied basic civil rights.

clue_en: This word is the opposite of shame and names many LGBTQ marches and festivals.
explanation_en: In the context of LGBTQ culture, LGBTQ pride (also known as queer pride, gay pride, or simply pride) is the promotion of the rights, self-affirmation, dignity, equality, and increased visibility of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ) people as a social group. Pride, as opposed to shame and social stigma, is the predominant outlook that bolsters most LGBTQ rights movements.

clue_en: In LGBTQ shorthand, 'ace' usually names which orientation involving little or no sexual attraction?
explanation_en: Asexuality is the lack of sexual attraction to others, or low or absent interest in or desire for sexual activity. It may be considered a sexual orientation, or the lack thereof.

clue_en: Someone says that neither of the two boxes 'man' and 'woman' fully describes their gender. Which identity may they use?
explanation_en: Non-binary (also written as nonbinary) or genderqueer gender identities are those that are outside the male/female gender binary. Non-binary identities often fall under the transgender umbrella since non-binary people typically identify with a gender that is different from the sex assigned to them at birth, although some non-binary people do not consider themselves transgender.

clue_en: Once chiefly a slur, this Q-word has been reclaimed as an umbrella identity by many people.
explanation_en: Queer is an umbrella term for sexual and gender minorities. It is alternately used to refer to people who reject sexual and gender norms and share radical politics characterized by solidarity across lines of identity.

clue_en: Kimberlé Crenshaw coined this term for overlapping systems of identity and discrimination.
explanation_en: Intersectionality is an analytical framework for understanding how groups' and individuals' social and political identities result in unique combinations of discrimination and privilege. Examples of these intersecting and overlapping factors include gender, caste, sex, race, ethnicity, class, sexuality, religion, disability, physical appearance, and age.

clue_en: This two-word phrase describes allowing same-sex couples to marry on the same terms as other couples.
explanation_en: Marriage equality means that same-sex couples may marry with the same legal status, rights, and responsibilities as other couples.

clue_en: This four-word U.S. military policy introduced in the 1990s barred openly gay, lesbian, and bisexual people from serving and was repealed in 2011.
explanation_en: Don't Ask, Don't Tell restricted openly gay, lesbian, and bisexual people from U.S. military service until its repeal took effect in 2011.

clue_en: This 2015 U.S. Supreme Court case required every state to license and recognize same-sex marriages.
explanation_en: Obergefell v. Hodges was the 2015 U.S. Supreme Court decision requiring states to license and recognize marriages between two people of the same sex.

clue_en: Voters in this 2015 national ballot made Ireland the first country to approve same-sex marriage by popular vote.
explanation_en: Ireland's 2015 marriage referendum approved same-sex marriage by popular vote, a first for a country-wide referendum.
source_title: Thirty-fourth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland — Wikipedia

clue_en: Malta became the first European country to enact this prohibition on attempts to change a person's sexual orientation or gender identity in 2016.
explanation_en: Malta's 2016 law prohibited conversion practices intended to change or suppress sexual orientation or gender identity.

clue_en: Celie tells her story in letters in this Alice Walker novel.
explanation_en: In Alice Walker's The Color Purple, Celie tells her life through letters and finds dignity and independence despite abuse.

clue_en: Oscar Wilde's only novel centers on a portrait that ages in its subject's place.
explanation_en: In Oscar Wilde's The Picture of Dorian Gray, Dorian stays young while his portrait ages and bears the marks of his actions.
source_title: The Picture of Dorian Gray — Wikipedia

clue_en: E. M. Forster wrote this novel about a young Englishman who falls in love with Clive and later Alec; it was published after Forster's death.
explanation_en: E. M. Forster's Maurice follows its title character's relationships with Clive Durham and Alec Scudder and was published posthumously in 1971.

clue_en: The English umbrella term for certain culturally specific Indigenous North American gender and spiritual roles begins with the number after one.
explanation_en: Two-Spirit is an umbrella term used by some Indigenous North American people for culturally specific gender, social, and spiritual roles.

clue_en: Judith Butler linked this two-word concept to gender being produced through repeated social acts.
explanation_en: Gender performativity, associated with Judith Butler, treats gender as produced through repeated acts and social conventions.

clue_en: A brick wall, microphone, and stand-up acts are stereotypical features of this venue.
explanation_en: A comedy club is a venue where a variety of comedic acts perform to a live audience. Although the term usually refers to establishments that feature stand-up comedians, it can also feature other forms of comedy such as improvisational comedians, impersonators, impressionists, magicians and ventriloquists.

clue_en: Liza Minnelli sings at Berlin's Kit Kat Club in this 1972 musical film.
explanation_en: In the 1972 musical film Cabaret, Liza Minnelli's Sally Bowles performs at Berlin's Kit Kat Club.

clue_en: A Sunset Strip building with a black exterior and a wall of comedians' names houses this stand-up club.
explanation_en: The Comedy Store is a stand-up club on the Sunset Strip whose black exterior bears the names of associated comedians.

clue_en: Tina Fey and Steve Carell trained at this Chicago improvisational theater.
explanation_en: The Second City is an improvisational comedy enterprise. It is the oldest improvisational theater troupe to be continuously based in Chicago, with training programs and live theaters in Toronto and New York.

clue_en: The Ramones and Blondie helped make this Bowery club a landmark of New York punk.
explanation_en: CBGB was a club on New York's Bowery whose stage became closely associated with punk bands including Ramones and Blondie.

clue_en: Tiny mirrors on this hanging sphere scatter spots of light across a dance floor.
explanation_en: A disco ball is a mirrored sphere that reflects moving spots of light around a dance venue.

clue_en: Coins, a numbered song list, and a glowing cabinet let bar patrons choose the next record on this machine.
explanation_en: A jukebox is a coin-operated music machine that lets a customer select a recording from a numbered list.

clue_en: Steve Rubell and Ian Schrager opened this Manhattan nightclub in 1977.
explanation_en: Studio 54 opened in New York in 1977.

clue_en: This Paris music hall opened in 1869 and became a symbol of Belle Époque entertainment.
explanation_en: The Folies Bergère opened in Paris in 1869.

clue_en: This 19th-century theatrical form parodied opera, Shakespeare, and classical subjects.
explanation_en: Victorian burlesque mixed parody, music, and theatrical spectacle.

clue_en: A bob haircut, short skirt, and 1920s jazz-club style evoke this fashionable young woman.
explanation_en: A flapper was a fashionable young woman associated with 1920s dress, jazz, and changing social customs.

clue_en: Singers, comedians, dancers, and novelty acts shared the bill in this variety-theater tradition.
explanation_en: Vaudeville was a variety-entertainment form built from separate acts such as comedy, song, dance, and novelty performance.

clue_en: This Harlem nightclub featured major Black performers while maintaining segregated admission for much of its early history.
explanation_en: The Cotton Club was a prominent Harlem nightclub with discriminatory admission policies.

clue_en: A 1979 baseball promotion at Chicago's Comiskey Park carried this name.
explanation_en: Disco Demolition Night took place at Comiskey Park in 1979.

clue_en: Dada artists founded this Zurich venue in 1916.
explanation_en: Cabaret Voltaire became a birthplace of Dada in 1916.

clue_en: The Beatles played nearly 300 times at this Liverpool cellar venue.
explanation_en: The Beatles played the Cavern Club in Liverpool nearly 300 times between 1961 and 1963.

clue_en: Barry Manilow sang about a showgirl named Lola at this New York nightclub.
explanation_en: Barry Manilow's song Copacabana tells of showgirl Lola and bartender Tony at the New York nightclub of that name.

clue_en: The Doors were once the house band at this Sunset Strip rock club.
explanation_en: The Doors served as the house band at the Whisky a Go Go on Los Angeles's Sunset Strip in 1966.

clue_en: This castle-like hotel on Sunset Boulevard is known for Hollywood celebrity stories.
explanation_en: Chateau Marmont is a castle-like Sunset Boulevard hotel long associated with stories about Hollywood celebrities.

clue_en: Elton John made his celebrated 1970 U.S. debut at this West Hollywood club.
explanation_en: Elton John's acclaimed August 1970 performances at the Troubadour introduced him to a major U.S. music-industry audience.

clue_en: This word combines removing clothing with playful delay or suggestion.
explanation_en: Striptease is a staged performance built around gradual undressing.

clue_en: Chicago clubs gave their city's name to the early history of this four-on-the-floor dance genre.
explanation_en: House music is an electronic dance genre that developed in Chicago clubs during the 1980s.

clue_en: Comedy, theatrical parody, costumes, and teasing stage performance combine in this kind of show.
explanation_en: A burlesque show combines theatrical parody, comedy, costume, and stylized adult stage entertainment.

clue_en: What term described the illegal transport of alcohol by sea or across borders during U.S. Prohibition?
explanation_en: Rum-running was the illegal transport of alcohol during Prohibition.

clue_en: This Harlem venue began presenting its famous Amateur Night in 1934.
explanation_en: The Apollo Theater's Amateur Night began in 1934.

clue_en: A colored paper or plastic band around the wrist can prove admission to a club or festival.
explanation_en: Nightclubs and festivals use wristbands to show admission, age status, or access privileges at a glance.

clue_en: Roped-off tables and bottle service often mark a club area reserved for guests with this special three-letter status.
explanation_en: A VIP is a person given special access or privileges because of status, influence, or importance; clubs may reserve roped-off areas for such guests.

clue_en: 'No sneakers' might be part of this set of clothing rules.
explanation_en: A dress code is a set of rules, often written, with regard to what clothing groups of people must wear. Dress codes are created out of social perceptions and norms, and vary based on purpose, circumstances, and occasions.

clue_en: At a club entrance, this worker exchanges coats for numbered claim tickets.
explanation_en: A coat check attendant stores guests' outerwear and returns it when they present the matching claim ticket.

clue_en: A club may collect this at the door before a guest buys any drinks.
explanation_en: A cover charge is an entrance fee sometimes charged at bars, nightclubs, or restaurants. It is collected upon entry or as an additional charge on the bill.

clue_en: Orange juice and sparkling wine make this brunch cocktail named like a yellow flower.
explanation_en: A mimosa mixes sparkling wine with citrus juice, usually orange juice, and shares its name with the yellow mimosa flower.

clue_en: Tomato juice gives this brunch cocktail its red color.
explanation_en: A Bloody Mary is a cocktail containing vodka, tomato juice, and other spices and flavorings including Worcestershire sauce, hot sauces, garlic, herbs, horseradish, celery, olives, pickled vegetables, salt, black pepper, lemon juice, lime juice and celery salt. Some versions of the drink, such as the "surf 'n' turf" Bloody Mary, include shrimp and bacon as garnishes.

clue_en: Equal parts gin, sweet vermouth, and Campari make this bitter Italian cocktail.
explanation_en: A Negroni is an Italian cocktail traditionally made with equal parts gin, sweet vermouth, and Campari.

clue_en: Peru and Chile both claim versions of this brandy cocktail topped with foam.
explanation_en: A pisco sour is an alcoholic cocktail of Peruvian origin, which is made from pisco, a Peruvian brandy, with sour citrus juice and sweetener components. The Peruvian pisco sour includes Peruvian pisco with freshly squeezed lime juice, simple syrup, ice, egg white, and Angostura bitters.

clue_en: New Orleans claims this rye-or-cognac cocktail flavored with absinthe.
explanation_en: Sazerac is a local variation of a cognac or whiskey cocktail originally from New Orleans. It is named for the Sazerac de Forge et Fils brand of cognac brandy that originally served as its main ingredient.

clue_en: A four-on-the-floor beat and mirrored ball define this 1970s dance style.
explanation_en: Disco is a dance-music style and club culture that became globally popular in the 1970s and is marked by a steady four-on-the-floor beat.

clue_en: This lively partner dance developed from Cuban and Puerto Rican musical traditions.
explanation_en: Salsa is the name for Latin American dances that are danced to salsa music. Salsa is one of the most popular types of Latin dance that is practiced worldwide, and is typically danced with a partner, although there are elements of solo footwork as well.

clue_en: This partner dance and music style originated in the Dominican Republic.
explanation_en: Bachata is a dance and music genre that originated in the Dominican Republic.

clue_en: Pose-like movements inspired by fashion magazines define this ballroom dance style.
explanation_en: Voguing uses fashion-photography-inspired poses, hand movements, and angular lines and developed within ballroom culture.

clue_en: A popular origin story links this Harlem swing dance's name with Charles Lindbergh's 1927 Atlantic 'hop.'
explanation_en: Lindy Hop is a swing dance associated with Harlem; a popular name story links it to Charles Lindbergh's 1927 Atlantic flight.

clue_en: DJs and all-night dance clubs draw visitors to this Spanish island.
explanation_en: Ibiza became an international nightlife destination through large clubs and dance-music events featuring prominent DJs.

clue_en: Rooftop bars and the backpacker strip Khao San Road belong to this Thai capital.
explanation_en: Bangkok's nightlife includes rooftop bars and the hostels, restaurants, and late venues around Khao San Road.

clue_en: Late dinners and milongas keep this Argentine capital awake for tango.
explanation_en: Buenos Aires is known for late dinners and milongas, social events where people gather to dance tango.

clue_en: Live-music clubs line this New Orleans street just downriver from the French Quarter.
explanation_en: Frenchmen Street in New Orleans is known for live-music venues near the French Quarter.

clue_en: A former power station in Berlin houses this club famous for techno and a strict door policy.
explanation_en: Berghain is a Berlin nightclub in a former power station, internationally known for techno music.

clue_en: Headache and thirst the morning after drinking are classic signs of this condition.
explanation_en: A hangover is the after-effect of drinking alcohol; common symptoms include headache, thirst, fatigue, and nausea.

clue_en: A bartender announces this final chance to order before closing.
explanation_en: In a bar, a last call (last orders) is an announcement made shortly before the bar closes for the night, informing patrons of their last chance to buy alcoholic beverages. There are various means to make the signal, like ringing a bell, flashing the lights, or announcing verbally.

clue_en: This hyphenated event begins when the main concert, awards show, or wedding reception ends.
explanation_en: An after-party is a social event held after a main event such as a concert, awards ceremony, premiere, or wedding reception.

clue_en: This late public-transport service can replace a taxi after trains stop running.
explanation_en: Night service, sometimes also known as owl service, is a mode of public transport service operated during the night hours. As an intermediate approach – between providing full service around the clock and stopping services altogether – it provides more limited service during times of lower passenger volume, saving resources and allowing for maintenance on primary transportation systems.

clue_en: Jet lag and shift work can disrupt this roughly 24-hour biological cycle.
explanation_en: A circadian rhythm, or circadian cycle, is a natural oscillation that repeats roughly every 24 hours. Circadian rhythms can refer to any process that originates within an organism (i.e., endogenous) and responds to the environment (is entrained by the environment).

clue_en: Scout Finch narrates this Harper Lee novel about her lawyer father Atticus defending Tom Robinson.
explanation_en: Harper Lee's To Kill a Mockingbird is narrated by Scout Finch and follows Atticus Finch's defense of Tom Robinson.

clue_en: Offred narrates Margaret Atwood's dystopia of Gilead.
explanation_en: The Handmaid's Tale is Margaret Atwood's dystopian novel about Offred's life under the patriarchal regime of Gilead.

clue_en: A 1989 fatwa against Salman Rushdie followed publication of this novel.
explanation_en: After The Satanic Verses was published, Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued a 1989 fatwa calling for Salman Rushdie's death.

clue_en: A U.S. court decision in 1933 cleared this James Joyce novel of obscenity.
explanation_en: In the 1933 United States v. One Book Called Ulysses decision, a federal court ruled that James Joyce's Ulysses was not obscene.

clue_en: Angie Thomas wrote this frequently challenged novel about Starr Carter witnessing a police shooting.
explanation_en: The Hate U Give is Angie Thomas's novel about Starr Carter, who witnesses the police shooting of her friend.

clue_en: In the U.S. system, these two letters mean parental guidance is suggested.
explanation_en: In the U.S. film-rating system, PG means parental guidance is suggested because some material may not be suitable for children.

clue_en: In U.S. cinemas, viewers under 17 need an accompanying adult for this rating.
explanation_en: In U.S. cinemas, an R-rated film requires viewers under 17 to attend with a parent or adult guardian.

clue_en: As of 2026, New Zealand uses this letter-and-number label for films restricted to viewers aged 18 and over.
explanation_en: In New Zealand's 2026 classification system, R18 restricts a film or publication to people aged 18 and over.

clue_en: This British board classifies films with labels such as U, PG, 12A, and 18.
explanation_en: The British Board of Film Classification assigns UK cinema and video labels including U, PG, 12A, 15, and 18.

clue_en: German cinema-goers see this three-letter age-rating body on posters and trailers.
explanation_en: The Freiwillige Selbstkontrolle der Filmwirtschaft (FSK, transl. Self-Regulatory Body of the Movie Industry) is a German motion picture rating system organization run by the Spitzenorganisation der Filmwirtschaft based in Wiesbaden.

clue_en: During a 1957 appearance, cameras framed Elvis Presley only from the waist up on this television variety program.
explanation_en: For Elvis Presley's third appearance on The Ed Sullivan Show in 1957, the broadcast showed him only from the waist up.

clue_en: MTV refused to air the original video for this 1990 Madonna single.
explanation_en: Madonna released 'Justify My Love' in 1990; MTV declined to broadcast its original music video.

clue_en: Obscenity arrests made this American stand-up comedian a free-speech symbol.
explanation_en: Lenny Bruce became a free-speech symbol after repeated obscenity arrests over language used in his stand-up performances.

clue_en: Chinese authorities detained this artist and government critic in 2011; he also created Tate Modern's Sunflower Seeds.
explanation_en: Chinese authorities detained Ai Weiwei for 81 days in 2011; the artist and government critic also created Tate Modern's Sunflower Seeds installation.

clue_en: Apartheid authorities banned several novels by this South African Nobel laureate.
explanation_en: South African apartheid authorities banned several novels by Nobel laureate Nadine Gordimer, including A World of Strangers and Burger's Daughter.

clue_en: Michelangelo painted this vast biblical scene behind the altar of the Sistine Chapel.
explanation_en: The Last Judgment is Michelangelo's large fresco on the altar wall of the Sistine Chapel.

clue_en: Marcel Duchamp submitted a signed urinal under this ironic title in 1917.
explanation_en: Fountain was a readymade sculpture attributed to Marcel Duchamp in 1917, consisting of a porcelain urinal signed "R. Mutt". The work is regarded by art historians and theorists of the avant-garde as a major landmark in 20th-century art.

clue_en: Andres Serrano photographed a small plastic crucifix submerged in amber liquid for this controversial 1987 work.
explanation_en: Andres Serrano's 1987 photograph Piss Christ depicts a small plastic crucifix submerged in a container of the artist's urine.

clue_en: John Singer Sargent repainted a fallen shoulder strap after this portrait caused a scandal in Paris.
explanation_en: Madame X is John Singer Sargent's portrait whose original fallen shoulder strap contributed to a Paris scandal.

clue_en: Judy Chicago's installation arranges symbolic place settings for women from history around a triangular table.
explanation_en: The Dinner Party is an installation artwork by American feminist artist Judy Chicago. There are 39 elaborate place settings on a triangular table for 39 mythical and historical famous women.

category_name_en: Freedom of Speech in Everyday Life
clue_en: In the United States, this amendment protects speech, press, religion, assembly, and petition.
explanation_en: The First Amendment (Amendment I) to the United States Constitution prevents Congress from making laws respecting an establishment of religion; prohibiting the free exercise of religion; or abridging the freedom of speech, the freedom of the press, the freedom of peaceable assembly and the right to petition the government for redress of grievances.

category_name_en: Freedom of Speech in Everyday Life
clue_en: The Onion and political cartoons use this form of humor to criticize people or institutions.
explanation_en: Satire is a genre of the visual, literary, and performing arts, usually in the form of fiction and less frequently non-fiction, in which vices, follies, abuses, and shortcomings are held up to ridicule, often with the intent of exposing or shaming the perceived flaws of individuals, corporations, government, or society itself into improvement.

category_name_en: Freedom of Speech in Everyday Life
clue_en: This person exposes wrongdoing inside an organization, sometimes at personal risk.
explanation_en: Whistleblowing (also whistle-blowing or whistle blowing) is the activity of a person, often an employee, revealing information about activity within a private or public organization that is deemed wrongful – whether it be illegal, immoral, illicit, unsafe, unethical, or fraudulent. Whistleblowers can communicate in a variety of ways internally, and/or publicly.

category_name_en: Freedom of Speech in Everyday Life
clue_en: Libel and slander are the written and spoken forms of this harm to reputation.
explanation_en: Defamation is communication that harms another person's reputation; its exact legal definition and the distinction between libel and slander vary by jurisdiction.

category_name_en: Freedom of Speech in Everyday Life
clue_en: A court may issue this order requiring someone to stop an action, including a planned publication.
explanation_en: An injunction is a court order requiring a party to do or stop doing a specified act; it can be sought to prevent publication.

clue_en: Firemen burn books in this Ray Bradbury novel whose title names paper's supposed ignition temperature in Fahrenheit.
explanation_en: Fahrenheit 451 is a 1953 dystopian novel by American writer Ray Bradbury. It presents a future American society where books have been outlawed and "firemen" burn any that are found.

clue_en: Schools have challenged this children's series about two pranksters and their superhero principal.
explanation_en: Captain Underpants is Dav Pilkey's children's series about two prank-loving boys and a principal who becomes their superhero creation.

clue_en: The BBC restricted this 1983 Frankie Goes to Hollywood single despite its cheerful one-word title.
explanation_en: Frankie Goes to Hollywood released 'Relax' in 1983; the BBC restricted the song from its radio and television outlets.

clue_en: Country stations boycotted this band after Natalie Maines criticized President George W. Bush in 2003.
explanation_en: U.S. country radio stations boycotted the Dixie Chicks after Natalie Maines criticized President George W. Bush in 2003.

clue_en: An American obscenity trial in 1957 centered on this Allen Ginsberg poem.
explanation_en: Allen Ginsberg's poem 'Howl' was the subject of a 1957 obscenity trial in San Francisco.

clue_en: Unwanted bulk email shares its name with a canned meat.
explanation_en: Email spam, also referred to as junk email, spam mail, or simply spam, refers to unsolicited messages sent in bulk via email. The term originates from a Monty Python sketch, where the name of a canned meat product,"Spam," is used repetitively, mirroring the intrusive nature of unwanted emails.

clue_en: These settings let adults limit what children can watch, play, or open online.
explanation_en: Parental controls are features which may be included in digital television services, computers and video games, mobile devices and software to enable parents to restrict certain content viewable by their children. This may be content they deem inappropriate for their age, maturity level or feel is aimed more at an adult audience.

clue_en: Opening or blacking out soldiers' letters during wartime is an example of this practice.
explanation_en: Postal censorship is official inspection of mail; during wartime it can involve opening letters or blacking out passages before delivery.

clue_en: A streaming service uses this technique when a show is available in one country but not another.
explanation_en: Geoblocking restricts access to online content according to the user's geographic location.

clue_en: In the United States, this movie preview may advertise restricted films to age-appropriate audiences.
explanation_en: A red-band trailer in the United States may preview restricted material for an age-appropriate audience.
source_title: Motion Picture Association film rating system — trailer ratings

clue_en: This notice alerts viewers that upcoming text may reveal a plot twist or ending.
explanation_en: A spoiler warning alerts an audience before a description reveals an important plot event, twist, climax, or ending.

clue_en: This short notice prepares an audience for potentially upsetting material.
explanation_en: A content warning is a notice that alerts an audience before material that may be disturbing or sensitive.

clue_en: Live television may use a few seconds of this so offensive language can be muted.
explanation_en: Broadcast delay inserts a short intentional gap into a live radio or television feed so mistakes or unacceptable material can be stopped before transmission.

clue_en: British broadcasters use this term for the time after which adult TV content may air.
explanation_en: In broadcasting, the watershed is the time after which programs intended only for mature audiences may be shown.

clue_en: Hollywood films followed this production code from the 1930s until the modern U.S. ratings system replaced it.
explanation_en: The Motion Picture Production Code, widely called the Hays Code, governed major-studio films in the United States from 1934 to 1968.

clue_en: A lawyer says this word to challenge a question or piece of evidence during a trial.
explanation_en: In the law of the United States of America, an objection is a formal protest to evidence, argument, or questions that are in violation of the rules of evidence or other procedural law. Objections are often raised in court during a trial to disallow a witness's testimony, and may also be raised during depositions and in response to written discovery.

clue_en: Guilty or not guilty are possible forms of this decision by a jury.
explanation_en: In law, a verdict is the formal finding of fact made by a jury on matters or questions submitted to the jury by a judge. In a bench trial, the judge's decision near the end of the trial is simply referred to as a finding.

clue_en: This court order requires a person to appear and testify as a witness.
explanation_en: A subpoena ad testificandum, also called a witness summons, compels a person to appear and testify before a court or other authority.

clue_en: Disobeying a judge or disrupting proceedings can lead to this finding.
explanation_en: Contempt of court covers conduct that disobeys a court order or shows serious disrespect for the court, including deliberate disruption of proceedings.

clue_en: Latin for 'friend of the court,' this filing offers information from someone outside the case.
explanation_en: An amicus curiae (lit. 'friend of the court'; pl. amici curiae) is an individual or organization that is not a party to a legal case, but that is permitted to assist a court by offering information, expertise, or insight that has a bearing on the issues in the case. Whether an amicus brief will be considered is typically under the court's discretion.

clue_en: Before publication, this newsroom worker verifies names, dates, quotations, and other claims in a story.
explanation_en: A fact-checker verifies factual claims in text prepared for publication, including names, dates, and quotations.

clue_en: Watching a movie for violence, language, and other content precedes this process of assigning its audience age label.
explanation_en: Film classification evaluates a film's content and assigns an age label or certificate describing its suitability for audiences.
source_title: Motion picture content rating system — Wikipedia

clue_en: This professional selects and interprets objects for an exhibition.
explanation_en: A museum curator selects objects for an exhibition and develops the interpretation that connects them for visitors.

clue_en: A streaming platform may use this step-by-step computer process to recommend your next show.
explanation_en: A streaming recommendation algorithm applies a defined sequence of calculations to viewing and preference data to suggest another program.

clue_en: At a U.S. television network, this department reviews programs for legal, ethical, and taste concerns.
explanation_en: In the United States, Standards and Practices (also referred to as Broadcast Standards and Practices or BS&P for short) is the name traditionally given to the department at a television network which is responsible for the moral, ethical, and legal implications of the program that the network airs.

clue_en: Botticelli painted Venus arriving on a giant shell in this Renaissance work.
explanation_en: Sandro Botticelli painted The Birth of Venus in the 1480s, showing the goddess Venus arriving at shore on a giant shell.

clue_en: This armless ancient Greek statue is displayed in the Louvre.
explanation_en: The Venus de Milo or Aphrodite of Melos is an ancient Greek marble sculpture that was created during the Hellenistic period. Its exact dating is uncertain, but the modern consensus places it in the 2nd century BC, perhaps between 160 and 110 BC. It was discovered in 1820 on the island of Milos, Greece, and has been displayed at the Louvre Museum since 1821.

clue_en: Jeff Koons made this giant mirror-bright sculpture resemble a party balloon animal.
explanation_en: Balloon Dog is Jeff Koons's monumental stainless-steel sculpture shaped like a balloon animal.

clue_en: Leonardo drew this man in a circle and square to study human proportions.
explanation_en: Leonardo da Vinci drew Vitruvian Man around 1490, showing a man in two superimposed positions within a circle and a square.

clue_en: This ancient Greek statue freezes an athlete just before he releases a discus.
explanation_en: The Discobolus by Myron ("discus thrower", Greek: Δισκοβόλος, Diskobólos) is an ancient Greek sculpture completed at the start of the Classical period in around 460–450 BC that depicts an ancient Greek athlete throwing a discus.

category_name_en: Famous Pairs and Symbols in Art
clue_en: Robert Indiana stacked two pairs of letters, tilting the O, in this famous sculpture design.
explanation_en: LOVE is Robert Indiana's four-letter image and sculpture design with a tilted O.

category_name_en: Famous Pairs and Symbols in Art
clue_en: A pitchfork-holding farmer stands beside a woman in Grant Wood's famous painting.
explanation_en: Grant Wood painted American Gothic in 1930 in the American Regionalist style. The figures stand before a Carpenter Gothic house, and Wood painted the work in oil on beaverboard.

category_name_en: Famous Pairs and Symbols in Art
clue_en: Gold leaf shimmers around an embracing couple in this Gustav Klimt painting.
explanation_en: The Kiss (German: Der Kuss) is an oil-on-canvas painting with added gold leaf, silver and platinum by the Austrian Symbolist painter Gustav Klimt. It was painted at some point in 1907 and 1908, during the height of what scholars call his "Golden Period".

category_name_en: Famous Pairs and Symbols in Art
clue_en: René Magritte hid a kissing couple's faces beneath white cloth in this surreal painting.
explanation_en: René Magritte painted The Lovers in 1928. It shows two people kissing while white cloth covers both faces.

category_name_en: Famous Pairs and Symbols in Art
clue_en: Rodin sculpted an embracing couple under this seasonal title.
explanation_en: Eternal Springtime (French: L'Éternel Printemps) is a c. 1884 sculpture by the French artist Auguste Rodin, depicting a pair of lovers.

clue_en: This Roman love god carries a bow and arrows.
explanation_en: In classical mythology, Cupid (Latin: Cupīdō, meaning "passionate desire") is the god of desire, erotic love, attraction and affection.

clue_en: This Greek goddess of love was said to rise from sea foam.
explanation_en: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty; one tradition says she arose from sea foam.

clue_en: Her face was said to launch a thousand ships in the Trojan War.
explanation_en: Helen of Troy was famed in Greek myth for extraordinary beauty; her abduction or elopement helped trigger the Trojan War and inspired the phrase about a face that launched a thousand ships.

clue_en: This mythic youth fell in love with his own reflection and inspired a psychology term.
explanation_en: In Greek myth, Narcissus became absorbed by his own reflection. His name gave rise to the psychology term narcissism.

clue_en: This beautiful youth loved by Aphrodite gave English a word for a handsome man.
explanation_en: Adonis was a beautiful mortal youth loved by Aphrodite in Greek myth; in English, an adonis can mean a very handsome young man.

clue_en: Anastasia Steele and Christian Grey lead this bestselling novel.
explanation_en: Fifty Shades of Grey is a 2011 erotic romance novel by British author E. L. James. It became the first installment in the Fifty Shades novel series that follows the deepening relationship between a college graduate, Anastasia Steele, and a young business magnate, Christian Grey.

clue_en: Humbert Humbert narrates this controversial Vladimir Nabokov novel.
explanation_en: Lolita is Vladimir Nabokov's novel narrated by the fictional Humbert Humbert.

clue_en: Pilgrims tell earthy stories while traveling to an English shrine in this Chaucer work.
explanation_en: Geoffrey Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales collects 24 stories told by pilgrims traveling from London to Saint Thomas Becket's shrine at Canterbury Cathedral.

clue_en: Boccaccio's storytellers pass time during the Black Death in this Italian collection.
explanation_en: Giovanni Boccaccio's 14th-century Decameron collects 100 stories told by 10 young Florentines sheltering from the plague.

clue_en: Letters reveal the schemes of Valmont and the Marquise de Merteuil in this French novel.
explanation_en: Pierre Choderlos de Laclos's 1782 epistolary novel Dangerous Liaisons depicts the manipulative schemes of Valmont and the Marquise de Merteuil.

clue_en: Monet and Renoir used visible brushstrokes to capture changing light in this movement.
explanation_en: Impressionism was a 19th-century art movement characterised by visible brush strokes, open composition, emphasis on accurate depiction of light in its changing qualities (often accentuating the effects of the passage of time), ordinary subject matter, unusual visual angles, and inclusion of movement as a crucial element of human perception and experience.

clue_en: This movement prized emotion, nature, and imagination over strict reason.
explanation_en: Romanticism (also known as the Romantic movement or Romantic era) was an artistic and intellectual movement that originated in Europe towards the end of the 18th century. The purpose of the movement was to advocate for the importance of subjectivity, imagination, and appreciation of nature in society and culture in response to the Age of Enlightenment and the Industrial Revolution.

clue_en: Flowing plant-like lines characterize this decorative style around 1900.
explanation_en: Art Nouveau was an international decorative style around 1900, recognized for flowing lines and forms inspired by plants and flowers.

clue_en: Henri Matisse and André Derain used intense non-natural colors in this early modern movement.
explanation_en: Fauvism was an early twentieth-century art movement associated with Henri Matisse, André Derain, and bold non-natural color.

clue_en: Rossetti and Millais belonged to this British group that looked back before Raphael.
explanation_en: The Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood was founded in 1848 by seven artists and writers who sought detailed color and composition inspired by art before Raphael.

clue_en: A white dress billows above a subway grate in a famous image of this star.
explanation_en: The famous white-dress image comes from a scene in the 1955 film The Seven Year Itch in which a subway draft lifts Marilyn Monroe's skirt above a Manhattan grate.
source_title: White dress of Marilyn Monroe — Wikipedia

clue_en: Apollo 8 photographed our blue planet above the Moon's horizon in this 1968 image.
explanation_en: Earthrise is a photograph of Earth taken from lunar orbit by astronaut William Anders on December 24, 1968, during the Apollo 8 mission. Nature photographer Galen Rowell described it as "the most influential environmental photograph ever taken".

clue_en: Eleven workers eat on a steel beam high above Manhattan in this 1932 photo.
explanation_en: Lunch atop a Skyscraper is a black-and-white photograph taken on September 20, 1932, of eleven ironworkers sitting on a steel beam of the RCA Building, 850 feet (260 meters) above the ground during the construction of Rockefeller Center in Manhattan, New York City. It was a staged photograph arranged as a publicity stunt, part of a campaign promoting the skyscraper.

clue_en: Green eyes stare from the 1985 National Geographic cover known by this title.
explanation_en: Afghan Girl is a 1984 photographic portrait of Sharbat Gula, an Afghan refugee in Pakistan during the Soviet–Afghan War. The photograph, taken by American photojournalist Steve McCurry near the Pakistani city of Peshawar, appeared on the June 1985 cover of National Geographic.

clue_en: A sailor kisses a woman in white in this 1945 celebration photograph.
explanation_en: V-J Day in Times Square is a photograph by Alfred Eisenstaedt that portrays a U.S. Navy sailor kissing a total stranger after grabbing her on Victory over Japan Day ("V-J Day") in New York City's Times Square on August 14, 1945.
source_title: V-J Day in Times Square — Wikipedia

clue_en: ABBA songs tell the story of Sophie and her three possible fathers in this jukebox musical.
explanation_en: Mamma Mia! is a jukebox musical built from ABBA songs. Its story follows Sophie as she invites three men who might be her father to her wedding.

clue_en: Tony and Maria fall in love amid rival New York gangs in this musical.
explanation_en: West Side Story adapts Romeo and Juliet to rival gangs in New York; Tony and Maria fall in love across the conflict between the Jets and Sharks.

clue_en: A masked musical genius haunts a Paris opera house in this Andrew Lloyd Webber show.
explanation_en: The Phantom of the Opera is a musical by Andrew Lloyd Webber about a masked musical genius who haunts the Paris Opera House and becomes obsessed with singer Christine Daaé.
source_title: The Phantom of the Opera — Wikipedia

clue_en: Bohemian friends in New York's East Village sing 'Seasons of Love' in this musical.
explanation_en: Rent follows young artists in New York's East Village during the HIV/AIDS crisis and includes the ensemble song 'Seasons of Love.'

clue_en: Orpheus and Eurydice descend into an industrial underworld in this folk-and-jazz musical.
explanation_en: Hadestown is Anaïs Mitchell's musical retelling of the myths of Orpheus, Eurydice, Hades, and Persephone.

clue_en: Ryan Gosling and Rachel McAdams play Noah and Allie in this romantic drama.
explanation_en: The Notebook is a romantic drama film starring Ryan Gosling and Rachel McAdams as Noah and Allie.

clue_en: Baby and Johnny practice a lift at a Catskills resort in this 1987 film.
explanation_en: Dirty Dancing is a 1987 American romantic drama dance film written by Eleanor Bergstein, produced by Linda Gottlieb, and directed by Emile Ardolino. Starring Patrick Swayze and Jennifer Grey, it tells the story of Frances "Baby" Houseman (Grey), a young woman who falls in love with dance instructor Johnny Castle (Swayze) while vacationing at a Borscht Belt resort in 1963.

clue_en: Rick tells Ilsa they will always have Paris in this wartime film.
explanation_en: In Casablanca, Rick and Ilsa are former lovers whose Paris history is recalled in the line “We'll always have Paris.”

clue_en: Heath Ledger and Jake Gyllenhaal play two cowboys whose relationship spans years in this film.
explanation_en: Brokeback Mountain stars Heath Ledger and Jake Gyllenhaal as two cowboys whose relationship begins while herding sheep in Wyoming.

clue_en: A New Year's Eve confession follows years of friendship in this romantic comedy.
explanation_en: When Harry Met Sally... follows Harry and Sally from friendship toward romance, culminating in Harry's New Year's Eve declaration.

clue_en: Pride and Prejudice brings together this witty heroine and proud estate owner.
explanation_en: Pride and Prejudice brings together Elizabeth Bennet and the initially proud Fitzwilliam Darcy through misunderstanding, reflection, and changed judgment.
source_title: Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy — Wikipedia

clue_en: A green light across the bay symbolizes his longing for her in The Great Gatsby.
explanation_en: The Great Gatsby  is a 1925 tragedy novel by American writer F. Scott Fitzgerald. Set in the Jazz Age on Long Island, near New York City, the novel depicts first-person narrator Nick Carraway's interactions with Jay Gatsby, a mysterious millionaire obsessed with reuniting with his former lover, Daisy Buchanan.
source_title: Daisy Buchanan and Jay Gatsby — Wikipedia

clue_en: A governess falls for the master of Thornfield Hall in Charlotte Brontë's novel.
explanation_en: Jane Eyre and Edward Rochester are the central couple of Charlotte Brontë's Jane Eyre, whose relationship is tested by the secret at Thornfield Hall.
source_title: Jane Eyre and Mr Rochester — Wikipedia

clue_en: Gone with the Wind follows the stormy relationship of these two Southerners.
explanation_en: In Gone with the Wind, Scarlett O'Hara and Rhett Butler form a turbulent relationship during and after the American Civil War.
source_title: Scarlett O'Hara and Rhett Butler — Wikipedia

clue_en: The windswept moors frame this doomed pair in Wuthering Heights.
explanation_en: In Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights, Catherine Earnshaw and the fostered orphan Heathcliff form the novel's central, destructive love relationship across the Yorkshire moors.

clue_en: New Yorkers often call this Fifth Avenue institution simply 'the Met.'
explanation_en: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, colloquially referred to as the Met, is an encyclopedic art museum in New York City.
source_title: The Metropolitan Museum of Art — Wikipedia

clue_en: Velázquez's Las Meninas is a treasure of this Madrid museum.
explanation_en: The Prado Museum in Madrid holds Diego Velázquez's Las Meninas as one of its defining works.

clue_en: A former Paris railway station houses this museum rich in Impressionist art.
explanation_en: Paris's Musée d'Orsay occupies the former Gare d'Orsay railway station and is especially known for its Impressionist collection.

clue_en: Botticelli's Birth of Venus hangs in this Florence gallery.
explanation_en: Florence's Uffizi Gallery houses Sandro Botticelli's The Birth of Venus.

clue_en: Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring hangs in this museum in The Hague.
explanation_en: The Mauritshuis in The Hague houses Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue_en: This worker mixes drinks and keeps the bar running.
explanation_en: A bartender prepares and serves alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks behind a bar.

clue_en: This licensed driver may take late-night passengers home for a metered fare.
explanation_en: A taxi driver transports passengers for a fare; local rules commonly govern driver licensing and the use of taximeters.

clue_en: This person queues backing tracks and calls singers to the microphone during a karaoke night.
explanation_en: A karaoke host runs a karaoke event by managing songs, performers, and the order of appearances.

clue_en: After a late show, this crew member moves scenery, cables, and equipment behind the scenes.
explanation_en: A stagehand works behind the scenes moving scenery, equipment, and cables for performances.

clue_en: At a hotel, this overnight employee balances the day's accounts and helps guests.
explanation_en: A night auditor is an employee who works at the reception of a hotel during the course of the night shift. Apart from performing the usual duties of a hotel receptionist, the night auditor's main task is to perform accounting checks.

clue_en: This lamp on a pole illuminates roads and pavements at night.
explanation_en: A street light, light pole, lamp pole, lamppost, streetlamp, light standard, or lamp standard is a raised source of light on the edge of a road or path. Similar lights may be found on a railway platform.

clue_en: Glowing gas-filled tubes spell a business name in this bright street display.
explanation_en: In the signage industry, neon signs are electric signs lighted by long luminous gas-discharge tubes that contain rarefied neon or other gases. They are the most common use for neon lighting, which was first demonstrated in a modern form in December 1910 by Georges Claude at the Paris Motor Show.

clue_en: Taxis line up at this designated pickup place.
explanation_en: A taxi stand is a designated place where taxis queue for passengers.

clue_en: At any hour, a hospital's ambulance entrance leads to this department for urgent care.
explanation_en: A hospital emergency department provides urgent medical assessment and treatment around the clock.

clue_en: Yellow signs, waffles, and doors open through the night identify this U.S. diner chain.
explanation_en: Waffle House is an American restaurant chain known for round-the-clock service at most locations.

clue_en: This restaurant worker takes orders and brings food to the table.
explanation_en: Waiting staff (BrE), waiters (masc) / waitresses (fem), or servers (AmE) are those who work at a restaurant, a diner, or a bar and sometimes in private homes, attending to customers by supplying them with food and drink as requested. Waiting staff follow rules and guidelines determined by the manager.

clue_en: A customer may leave a tip after this professional cuts or styles their hair.
explanation_en: A hairdresser cuts and styles hair, and tipping is customary for the service in some countries.

clue_en: At the front of a walking group, this worker turns streets, monuments, or museum objects into stories.
explanation_en: A tourist guide is a person who guides visitors in the language of their choice and interprets the cultural and natural heritage of an area. Tourist guides normally possess an area-specific qualification, usually issued and/or recognised by the appropriate authority.

clue_en: At a hotel awning, a guest may exchange car keys for a claim ticket from this worker.
explanation_en: Valet parking is a service in which an attendant parks and later retrieves a customer's vehicle.

clue_en: A brass luggage cart, a hotel lobby, and a guest's room number are the working clues for this employee.
explanation_en: A bellhop (North America), or hotel porter (international), is a hotel employee who helps patrons with their luggage while checking in or out. Bellhops often wear a uniform, like certain other page boys or doormen.

clue_en: This small workplace label displays an employee's name for customers.
explanation_en: A name tag or name badge is a badge or sticker worn on the outermost clothing as a means of displaying the wearer's name for others to view. Name tags may be temporary, such as a sticker with a person's name, or it may be more durable.

clue_en: A refrigerator, kettle, and lockers may be found in this employee-only room.
explanation_en: A break room is a room in a workplace where employees can go during meals and other breaks.

clue_en: Hours worked beyond a normal schedule may receive extra pay under this term.
explanation_en: Overtime is the amount of time someone works beyond normal working hours. The term is also used for the pay received for this time.

clue_en: Hiring, benefits, and employee policies often belong to this department.
explanation_en: A human-resources department commonly manages recruitment, benefits, employee records, and workplace policies.

clue_en: Employees punch in and out on this device to record working hours.
explanation_en: A time clock, sometimes known as a clock card machine, punch clock, or time recorder, is a device that records start and end times for hourly employees (or those on flexi-time) at a place of business.
